newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Arcadia directors recommend Sipa offer.
newsitem.headline: Arcadia directors recommend Sipa offer.

text.p: Independent directors of Arcadia Minerals NL said on Tuesday they would now recommend that shareholders accept a takeover offer by Sipa Resources International NL, revising the recommendation in the formal Part B response to the offer dispatched on May 9.
The directors' statement followed Sipa's pro forma substantial shareholding notice earlier on Tuesday that it held 59.1 percent of Arcadia as of Friday, up from 57.5 percent on Thursday.
The Arcadia directors said the change of recommendation followed Sipa's extension of its offer to June 13.

"However, your independent directors have made a request to Sipa to further extend their offer to a date on or after 8 July 1997, and we are waiting an a response from Sipa in this regard," the Arcadia directors said in a statement.

They said that if the offer were extended to July 8, this would provide a more reasonable time period for shareholders to consider the revised recommendation of the independent directors, and it would provide the possibility of accepting the offer in either of the 1997 or 1999 tax years.

"The independent directors now intend to accept Sipa's offer in respect of their own shareholdings, only in the event that the offer is extended beyond 30 June 1997, for their own individual financial reasons," the statement said.

"Changed circumstances arising from the level of acceptances which Sipa has received to its offer, as well as share market factors, including share liquidity and the possible share prices of Arcadia after the after closes, have led to the independent directors revising their general recommendation to shareholders," the statement said.

"In weighing up the relevant factors in the context of the current circumstances, the independent directors now believe that the benefits arising from accepting Sipa's offer and becoming a shareholder of Sipa, a larger and more diverse company than Arcadia with greater share liquidity, should outweigh the benefits from remaining a shareholder of Arcadia."
Sipa raised its bid on May 5 to seven Sipa shares and 40 cents cash for every four Arcadia shares from the original five for three scrip offer.
Arcadia shares closed at A$1.04 on Friday, when they last traded. Sipa shares closed on Tuesday at 58 cents, down a cent.
Sipa and Arcadia are partners in the Dublin Hill gold joint venture in Western Australia.
The joint venture is 70 percent owned by Sipa and 30 percent by Arcadia.
